title: Building a Ten From Ones
objective: Connect Unit 1.3's Make 10 bridge (within 20) to place value — when ones reach 10, they become a new ten, linking the addition strategy to the base-ten system it depends on.
studentQuestion: You made a ten while adding before — what happens to it now that we're using tens and ones?
newIdea: None new procedurally — this lesson makes explicit the connection between Unit 1.3's 10 and Unit 2.1's 1 ten. This lesson also carries the two-digit Make-10 transfer example deferred from Unit 1.3 (see docs/foundation-release-1/README.md P2 Prerequisite Finding).

teaching.setup: 2 tens and 7 ones, with 5 more loose ones being added (mirrors a Unit 1.3 bridge: 7 + 5).
teaching.see: We have 7 loose ones, and we're adding 5 more. What happened last time this came up?
teaching.break: Bridge the 7 ones to 10 using the familiar split (5 = 3 + 2).
teaching.build: The 10 ones formed this way get bundled into a brand-new ten.
teaching.transform: 2 tens plus the newly bundled ten plus 2 leftover ones — 3 tens and 2 ones (32) — Make 10 and the tens/ones system shown as one connected idea.

check.prompt: Unbundle everything and count all loose ones to confirm 32.

examples.transfer: 49 + 3 = 52 (crossing not just to a new ten but into a new tens digit territory).

mastery.evidence: Correctly solves 2 two-digit-plus-single-digit bridging problems and reports the full two-digit answer.
